title: Transfer pricing basics for cross-border transaction disputes
p1:
A company can follow every contract rule and still face a tax dispute across borders.

Why? Because different countries may disagree on whether the price charged between related companies is fair.
p2:
A common misconception is that transfer pricing is only about setting prices. In reality, it is about proving that cross-border transactions happen as if the companies were independent.

A surprising fact: even a small difference in pricing between group companies can create large tax adjustments when transactions involve millions of dollars.
p3:
Transfer pricing rules ask a simple question: Would an unrelated company agree to the same terms?

For example, if a parent company sells services to its overseas subsidiary, tax authorities may review whether the service fee reflects a market-based value.

The practical takeaway: good documentation is often the difference between a smooth review and a costly dispute. Companies should be ready to explain the business reason behind their pricing decisions.
conclusion: When companies operate across borders, what factors do you think create the biggest transfer pricing disputes: pricing, documentation, or differences between tax authorities?
